gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-009 concerns an invalid uniform-in-all-larger-sample-sizes quantifier for selected eigenpair labels. It does not recognize that the introductory spectrum-convergence wording overstates conditional subsequential results whose exact-eigenpair identification requires a nonzero weak limit.

ISSUE-001 diagnoses non-well-definedness of an empirical operator on sampled-value equivalence classes. The gold issue concerns composition by an arbitrary flow on almost-everywhere L-infinity equivalence classes and the missing null-set preservation hypothesis; the mathematical objects and obligation differ.

Both identify that the sampled-value representation is non-injective, so an empirically zero representative can have a nonzero sampled image. Consequently the induced empirical operator is not well-defined and the projection/exact-approximation argument fails.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The induced operator on sampled-value equivalence classes is not well-defined because equality of sampled dictionary values does not imply equality of sampled operator values.

component_coverage.gold_component: Non-injective sampling makes the induced empirical operator fail to descend to sampled-value equivalence classes, invalidating the claimed empirical operator and dependent exact-approximation identity.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states the non-injective sampling implication that fails, gives the zero-class/nonzero-image consequence, and identifies the resulting undefined induced operator and invalid proof step.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that zero-mean dictionary and operator noise does not remove quadratic dictionary-noise covariance or the noise cross-covariance. Thus the empirical matrices concentrate around perturbed population matrices and the claimed consistency around A_N has persistent errors-in-variables bias.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The noisy Gram and cross-covariance matrices are centered at noise-perturbed population quantities, not at G_N and C_N, so concentration cannot establish convergence of the stated estimator to A_N.

component_coverage.gold_component: The assumed centered noise does not justify the population identities for the noisy Gram and cross matrices; covariance and cross-covariance terms remain and invalidate concentration around the noiseless matrices.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives both missing covariance terms, states that concentration is around the wrong matrices, and identifies the resulting persistent estimator bias.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the conditioning event as the intersection of M independent truncation events, whose probability is p-tilde_N^M rather than p-tilde_N. Therefore the claimed conversion to unconditional confidence is invalid and worsens with M.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof uses the probability of one truncation event where it needs the probability of the joint all-samples truncation event, causing an invalid confidence calibration.

component_coverage.gold_component: The all-sample truncation event has probability p-tilde_N^M, so multiplying or calibrating with only p-tilde_N does not establish the claimed unconditional confidence.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly counts all M independent noise vectors, gives the correct joint probability, derives the invalid probability relation, and notes the degradation as M grows.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-008 concerns the separate failure of boundedness of eigenvalues for unbounded operators. It does not identify the invalid inference from pointwise projection convergence for fixed g to norm convergence of (I-P_N)A f_N for a varying sequence, nor the pairing-based repair.
